{{Nihongo|'''Masaaki Morisita'''|森下正明光}} (27 January 1913 - 25 February 1997) was a Japanese ecologist and professor emeritus of animal ecology at [[Kyoto University]]. He is known as the father of [[population ecology]] in Japan. [[Morisita's overlap index]] and [[Taylor's law#Morisita’s index of dispersion|Morisita's index of dispersion]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Morisita |first1=Masaaki |title=I σ -Index, a measure of dispersion of individuals |journal=Population Ecology |date=December 1962 |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=1–7 |doi=10.1007/BF02533903}}</ref> are named after him.

In addition to his work on statistical ecology, he also studied the natural history of Japanese ants. With several other [[myrmecologist]]s, he produced a complete catalogue of ants in Japan.<ref name="obit">{{cite journal |last1=Morisita |first1=Masaaki |title=Obituary |journal=Population Ecology |date=June 1997 |volume=39 |issue=1 |pages=1–2 |doi=10.1007/BF02765243}}</ref> Three species of ants are named after him (''Pyramica morisitai'', ''[[Proceratium]] morisitai '', and ''Lasius morisitai'').

==Biography==
Morisita was born in [[Osaka]] and spent his high school years in [[Kōchi, Kōchi|Kōchi]]. He obtained a bachelor's of agriculture at Kyoto University in 1932, and later a doctorate of science in 1950.<ref name="obit"/> He studied the water strider ''[[Gerris lacustris]]'' as part of his graduate studies. After graduating, he worked as a professor in the department of biology at [[Kyushu University]]. He later became a professor in the zoology department of Kyoto University. In 1976, he retired and was named professor emeritus.

He published the book ''Studies on Methods of Estimating Population Density, Biomass, and Productivity in Terrestrial Animals'' in 1977.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Morisita |first1=Masaaki |title=Studies on methods of estimating population density, biomass, and productivity in terrestrial animals |date=1977 |publisher=University of Tokyo Press |language=en}}</ref>

He was awarded the Zoological Society of Japan Award in 1964, and the [[Order of the Rising Sun]], 3rd Class in 1986. After his death, the Morisita Memorial & Research Foundation was named in his honor.

==Name==
Like many academics from Kyoto University, Morisita had a preference for the spelling of his name in foreign language papers, writing it as "Morisita" using [[Kunrei-shiki romanization]], rather than the English-based [[Hepburn romanization]] "Morishita".
